summary: Tested per-destination tariffs (dest-rates API + DestRates panel), Zadarma compare dialog, weekly check endpoint, Chile number cost = 6, /admin/costs and /admin/monitor/margins regression. All requested flows work. 9/10 backend tests pass; one minor bug: DELETE /dest-rates/{code}/manual on unknown code creates junk entry.

minor.issue: No existence check: for unknown code (e.g. ZZ) when dest_rates doc exists, it creates rates.ZZ={manual:false} with no usd_min/name. Listed in GET response and UI (empty input). Worse: CR.line_rate does learned['usd_min'] -> KeyError if a junk entry matches a real region (e.g. reset on 'MX' before learned) -> 500 in /admin/costs and compare. Fix: 404 like PUT, and use learned.get('usd_min') in line_rate.
number_cl_usd_month Field default still 8.0 while DEFAULT_PRICING is 6.0; inconsistent if client omits field on PUT /admin/pricing.

issues: After 'reset' (Volver a la de Zadarma), origin label shows 'De Zadarma' but value stays the manual one (0.2) until next Zadarma learn — could mislead; consider a hint like 'se actualizará en la próxima sincronización'.
Dialog uses dark bg-slate-900 while the Costes page is light theme — visual inconsistency (readable though).

action_items: Add 404 check in reset_dest_rate for unknown codes and make CR.line_rate robust to entries missing usd_min
critical_code_review_comments: weekly_check marks week as done before running compare; if Zadarma errors transiently on Monday 9:00, that week's email is skipped silently (only a log line). Consider marking the week only on success/no-error.
monitor.py:393 CL 8->6 migration runs every loop iteration (cheap no-op, OK) but it will also override an admin that intentionally set exactly 8.0.
